explanation: Unlike the Middle East, South Asia, and parts of Africa — where the left hand is reserved for hygiene tasks and avoided at the table — Greece has no such taboo. Greeks eat in standard Continental style (fork in the left hand, knife in the right), and left-handed diners face no social penalty.
local_tip: Eat normally with whichever hand is comfortable; there's no left-hand rule in Greek dining, though keeping both hands visible above the table is good general manners.

also_check.note: The left hand is reserved for hygiene; always eat and pass food with the right hand.
The left hand is considered unclean, so food should be eaten and passed with the right hand.
Eating or passing food with the left hand is taboo in most traditional settings.

sources.title: Why Left-Handed Eating Is Frowned Upon In The Middle East
